rv.q: But if you're doing "Secret Garden" in a small space, simplicity is your byword and there's a lot of extra stuff going on here that does not always work.
Something musically magical is in bloom at Theo Ubique.

Director Christopher Pazdernik delivers a gorgeous, riveting rendition of librettist Marsha Norman ’s and composer Lucy Simon 's musical Garden based on the classic children’s novel published in 1911 by Frances Hodgson Burnett .
Theo Ubique’s alluring production is a timeless tale that blooms with the power of love.
This new, thoughtful Theo production, directed by Christopher Pazdernik, makes a strong argument that “The Secret Garden” should be revived more often.
Adding to the message and the storyline are the beautiful music and meaningful lyrics in a performance so well done and so emotionally engaging that it completely captures the audience.
At Theo, it has earned a respect as a marvelous holiday offering.
Theo’s solid staging of the novel’s musical adaptation (book and lyrics by Marsha Norman, score by Lucy Simon) reveals a tale that remains timeless.
The cast for this production is amazingly talented with voices that are pure magic.
This Tony and Drama Desk award-winning musical is for all ages, and soars in a compelling tale of forgiveness, love, hope, family, and renewal.

cn.t: Critics praise Theo Ubique's beautiful, intimate production of this timeless musical, calling it magical and heartwarming. Most laud the heartfelt performances and emotional depth, though one finds it needs more storefront intimacy.
